name: Incline Dumbbell Tricep Kickback
description: The incline dumbbell kickback is performed face-down on an incline bench, with the chest resting on the pad and the arms hanging. The incline position allows gravity to fully load the tricep in the extended (kickback) position — where standard kickbacks rely on a horizontal upper arm for resistance. By using an incline, the peak contraction in the extended position is better maintained. The prone position also eliminates any torso rocking.

execution.starting_position: Set an incline bench to 30-45 degrees. Lie face-down with the chest on the pad. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging down.
execution.setup_instructions: Use light dumbbells — the incline kickback is a strict isolation movement with limited leverage.
steps: Step 1: Begin with the arms hanging down, upper arms at the sides of the body.
Step 2: Extend the elbows rearward, kicking the dumbbells back behind the body.
Step 3: Hold at full extension for one second, squeezing the triceps.
Step 4: Return the dumbbells to the hanging position with control.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the kickback, inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Swinging the dumbbells using shoulder movement
Not fully extending the elbows at the peak
safety_considerations: The prone position limits cheating — keep the chest on the bench
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension at the top — pause and squeeze.
